status: draft - warm wording for Cory to review; follows docs/expert/VOICE_RULE.md. {placeholders} are filled by code from the report's own words.
not_performed: The report says this wasn't done: {topic}. Ask: What was the reason, and does it change what the report concludes?
not_checked: I couldn't check this part of the report: {detail} Ask the person who sent it for the original file.

dates_disagree.text: The report gives two different dates. Ask: Why was sampling on a different day than the inspection?
dates_disagree.why: Conditions can change between days, and results describe the day sampled.

two_lab_names.text: The report names more than one laboratory. Ask: Which lab analyzed which sample?
two_lab_names.why: Each result should trace to the lab that produced it.

defined_never_used.text: The report defines categories but doesn't say which one applies to any area. Ask: Which category does each area fall into?
defined_never_used.why: The categories only help if they are applied.

time_spans_differ.text: The report gives two different time spans for the same step. Ask: Which one applies?
time_spans_differ.why: A contractor will follow one, and the two lead to different waits.

result_contradicts_threshold.text: A result is labeled in a way that doesn't match the report's own line. Ask: Which is right, the label or the number?
result_contradicts_threshold.why: The label and the number should agree.

baseline_labeled_elevated.text: A reference reading is labeled elevated. Ask: Is it a baseline, or was it elevated?
baseline_labeled_elevated.why: A baseline is the comparison point for the rest.

narrative_material_without_reading.text: The report describes moisture on a material in a room, but the room's reading table doesn't list one. Ask: Was that material measured?
narrative_material_without_reading.why: A statement of moisture is easier to rely on with a reading beside it.

recommendation_without_measure_or_sample.text: In {area}, the report recommends work but doesn't show a reading or sample for that area. Ask: What supports the recommendation there?
recommendation_without_measure_or_sample.why: Work that is opened up or removed should rest on something measured or sampled.

cause_without_measure.text: In {area}, the report states a cause but doesn't show a reading for that area. Ask: What measurement points to that cause?
cause_without_measure.why: A cause is easier to rely on with a reading behind it.

conclusion_without_anything_behind_it.text: In {area}, the report draws a conclusion but doesn't show what was seen, measured or sampled there. Ask: What was the conclusion based on?
conclusion_without_anything_behind_it.why: Each conclusion should trace back to something in the report.
